name: Global food prices
summary: FAO food price index 133.9 in October, below the 135 Alert line but up 5.9% on a year; next release 4 Dec
state: The FAO Food Price Index averaged 133.9 points in October, down 1.2% on September but 5.9% above October 2025 (FAO; Food Ingredients First, 9 Nov). Sugar rose 6.6% on the month to its highest since December 2024, while cereals fell 4.5%. The annual rise meets the Watch line and the index stays below 135; searches on 15 Nov found India's rice exporters bracing for possible curbs on broken rice, but no staple export bans by several major exporters.
for_you: Households in import-dependent countries and lower-income households spend the largest share on food and are most exposed. In the UK, higher world prices tend to reach shop shelves over several months.
rubric_hit: Watch: FAO index y/y +5.9% > +5%; level 133.9 below the 135 Alert line

sources.title: Food Ingredients First — FAO food prices October 2026
S&P Global — Indian rice exporters brace for possible curbs on 100% broken rice exports

why: Food prices drive inflation, hunger and political unrest; poorer countries spend up to half of income on food.
drivers: Harvests, weather, fertiliser and energy costs, export bans, conflict in breadbaskets.

rubric.alert: FFPI > 135, or multiple major exporters ban exports of a staple.
rubric.watch: FFPI 120–135, or y/y > +5%, or a major exporter restricts exports.
rubric.normal: FAO Food Price Index < 120 and y/y change < +5%.
